questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to get far away from Denmark, to explore new cultures. I wanted an English speaking country, to not make it too difficult for myself, since I'm not that great in other foreign languages.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It would have been a 10, if it wasn't for the stress of applying to a new university and getting the courses I wanted to take approved by my host uni and KU

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It became easy to get help with stuff once I arrived, they had a great team helping international students

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had a great team that provided a lot of help and that you could text or talk  to if any help was necessary.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They also did a full week of welcome activities, so you quickly find friends that are in the same situation as you, that you can get help from

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, although I did only find housing 2 weeks before arriving. The school  helps you find off campus housing by telling you what to look out for, because there is some people that wanna scam you, but a lot of international students, including myself found a place to stay through facebook groups, since the school prefers people who study at the school for a full year, to be the ones that get on campus housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There's alot of busses around town, so public transport is quite easy. Just be aware that they stop driving at night. Other than that, just try and get a place near campus or downtown Victoria, but places further away are also fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's easy enough, but a bit stressfull. Make sure to apply for loads of courses and make sure they're in different "skema grupper", and that they teach those courses in the semester you're applying for.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There's a website, where you can match your courses and make sure they don't overlap, use that!! If something happens, you still have like a month from when you start, where you can change courses, but you have to have the new courses approved by KU as well, so make sure you apply for a lot of courses before you go.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can e-mail (takes a little while to get an answer back), call them or go talk with them, they are very helpfull

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was 1 course i was really hoping I would get, but I didn't get approved for it. other than that it was fine, and they have a lot of different options

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join some of their clubs, they have a lot, from sports to book clubs, they have sooo much, and it's a great way to make friends.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It's alot like "gymnasiet" in DK, with a lot of assignments, that all count for a small percentage of your final grade, which is a bit anoying. But I just needed to pass my classes, so when the final exams came, I had no stress, because I knew I already was going to pass. You can read about the classes and what the expectations are, so you can do whatever you want, but I recommend you take easy classes, so you can enjoy the free time with your new friends and nature

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Depends on the courses you take, you can choose what you want

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Geography for today: Geography of food
Our digital earth
Coastal Geography
AE303A - Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Technique

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
AE303A - Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Technique. 
You do pottery!! I was really bad at it, which was kind of scary, because the rest of the class was pretty good. But you have to remember it's an introductory class, so the bar is very low. You basically just have to hand in whatever and you will pass. One annoying thing though, was all the deadlines you have in that class, so you end up spending quite some time there, if you wanna make your stuff kinda pretty

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing prices is about the same as in copenhagen, but not as bad as in Vancouver. Food is expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i highly recommend joining a club or sport!! i did football and white water kayaking, where you go down "small" waterfalls in kayaks, which was really, really fun

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything.. all the clubs you can think of, and they have an orientation day, where you can go talk with them all. Every week they have some service dogs come visit the campus, that are there for you to pet and play with - great if you're feeling home sick or just want some love.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Victoria has some quite okay nightlife, although most stuff closes between 12 and 02. But you should definetely focus on renting cars and drive out into the wilderness! Go surfing at Tofino, climb mountains, go skiing, go see whales, orcas and sea otters

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and explore the island - it's way bigger than you think. You can also visit Vancouver about 5 hours away with public transport, less with a car. You can visit some of all the ski resorts. I Went to Cypress mountain for a day, near Vancouver and also took a bus to revelstoke (best skiing place in the world) during christmas to go ski there for a week. Visit Seattle for a weekend. fly or drive to Banff - can't recommend this enough. INSANE nature!! There's an airport in victoria that can take you there. Other trips a lot of exchange students and myself went from that airport include Mexico, Hawaii, LA, and Las Vegas. Flights to and from the states directly can be crazy cheap.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I think Canada in general is a lot like DK. They are very polite and you will get used to thanking the bus driver before leaving busses. One bad thing is the number of homeless people in cities. I've grown up in Vesterbro, but still got a bit shocked about how bad the opiod crisis is and how vissible the homeless are in the cities. But I never ran into an actual problem with the homeless, it's just different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club!! It can be hard to socialize in class, because most people just leave straight after class to go to a new one. UVic do invite all the exchange students to do a lot of socializing the week before school starts, so that helps you meet like minded people, that like yourself, will be trying to make new friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Tipping! Just prepare yourself to be paying 15-20% more than advertised.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their friendliness!! Such great people and they have also started preaching a lot about the first nation history (indigenous).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go with an open mind and be preparred to make friends. Make sure your social battery is charged! although, you of course decide for yourself, if you need a break. You might feel overwelmed with all the assignments, but the level isn't too bad and you will find yourself stress free at the final exams. Focus on making friends and exploring the wonderfull Vancouver island!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much, they are very nice and everything is going to work out fine

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I made, and the nature I explored with them

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting the right courses and getting them approved

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy - you're gonna love it!!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
